correctness.rationale: Pair indices -j,j+1 in the centered Zak sum at x=1/2 give 2 sqrt(lambda) exp(pi i nu) sum_{j=0}^3 B3(lambda(j+1/2)) cos((2j+1)pi nu), with nonzero pairs exhaustively split at 3/7 and 3/5. Dividing by cos(pi nu), y=cos²(pi nu), gives the specified cubic on (1/3,3/7), quadratic on [3/7,3/5), affine on [3/5,1). Verified the cubic expansion, discriminant 81(3lambda-1)^4D and strictly negative rational Bernstein coefficients of D on the entire interval, whence one real cubic root; its sign at y=0 changes only at lambda*=(99-2 sqrt(42))/247 and y=1 stays positive. Verified Q discriminant 4E with strictly negative Bernstein coefficients on [3/7,23/50] and positive remaining coefficients for larger scales; affine part has positive constant. Critical root at y=0 gives central zero of order 3 at lambda*, as also at lambda=1/2. Root y->1/4 at lambda down to 1/3. This establishes exactly 3 versus 1 distinct real frequencies for ALL real lambda in (1/3,1), not a numerical extrapolation.
